langCode.description: This translation's language code (en, de, pt_BR…), used as the page's lang attribute.

machineTranslatedTitle.description: Starts the note shown on Anubis's own pages in any language but English. Say that a machine made this translation.

machineTranslatedNote.message: A machine translated Anubis into your browser's language, and the translation isn't fully supported: some of it may be wrong or unclear, so use it with caution. To see Anubis in English, set your browser's language to English.
machineTranslatedNote.description: After machineTranslatedTitle, in Settings and on the welcome page, in any language but English.

machineTranslatedShort.description: After machineTranslatedTitle at the bottom of the toolbar popup, in any language but English: a short form of machineTranslatedNote.

machineTranslatedHelp.description: A link after the machine translation note, to the wiki page on translating Anubis.

extDescription.message: Weighs your search results: tag, rerank, and hide sites, with lists anyone can publish.
extDescription.description: Shown in the stores and the browser's add-ons page. At most 132 characters.

commandToggleEnabled.description: Keyboard shortcut, listed in the browser's shortcut settings.

commandToggleHidden.message: Show hidden results, or hide them again
commandToggleHidden.description: Keyboard shortcut, listed in the browser's shortcut settings.

levelHide.description: A site's ranking. The five rankings are Hide, Lower, Normal, Raise, and Pin.

levelPin.description: A site's ranking: always at the top.

popupOn.description: In the toolbar popup. Under the on/off switch while Anubis is on.

popupOff.message: Off. Search pages are left as they are.
popupOff.description: In the toolbar popup. Under the on/off switch while Anubis is off.

popupOnLabel.description: Screen reader label of the on/off switch.

popupAddSite.description: In the toolbar popup. A button and heading for adding a site by hand. Also in Settings → Your sites.

popupRanking.description: Screen reader label of the ranking menu next to Add a site.

popupNoSites.message: Nothing yet. Rank a site from the menu on any of its results.
popupNoSites.description: In the toolbar popup. Under “Your sites” (popupYourSites) while you’ve ranked none.

popupKeptNormal.description: A site set to Normal on purpose, overriding lists.

popupListsAndTags.description: $1 is the number of lists (popupListCount), $2 the number of tags (popupTagCount).

popupListCount_one.description: In the toolbar popup. At the foot: how many lists you subscribe to. Also in Settings.

popupTagCount_one.description: How many tags there are, in the toolbar popup and Settings.

popupRankingFor.description: Screen reader label; $1 is a site.

popupRankPin.message: Pin $1 to the top of search results

popupYourSites.description: Heading over the last few sites in your list, in the toolbar popup.

popupSeeAll.description: Opens Settings → Your sites. $1 is how many sites you've ranked.

popupOpenLists.description: In the toolbar popup. Tooltip of the list and tag count at the foot.

popupShowOnly.description: Heading over the tags on this page's results; choosing one shows only its results.

popupTags.description: Heading over a site’s tags, in the toolbar popup; also the Tags column in Settings → Your sites.

popupSite.description: Screen reader label of the menu that picks how much of a site a ranking covers.

popupSiteChoice.message: Choose how much of the site this applies to
popupSiteChoice.description: In the toolbar popup. Tooltip of the menu that picks how much of a site (fandom.com or harrypotter.fandom.com) a ranking applies to.

popupHintAllow.description: In the toolbar popup. Under the rankings, for a site you set to Normal on purpose.

popupHintMine.message: Your choice for $1, on every search.

popupHintMineTags.message: Your choice for $1, on every search, added to your tag settings.
popupHintMineTags.description: In the toolbar popup and the menu on a result. Under the rankings, for a site you ranked whose tags you set to Raise or Lower also move it. $1 is a site.

popupHintLists.message: $1 by $2. Choose one to decide yourself.
popupHintLists.description: $1 is a ranking in the past tense (Hidden, Raised…), $2 the lists that chose it.

popupHintNone.message: Your choice applies on every search.
popupHintNone.description: In the toolbar popup. Under the rankings, for a site you haven’t ranked.

popupYourTagSettings.description: Stands in for a list's name in popupHintLists when a tag you chose to hide or raise decided the ranking.

tagMarkRaise.description: What a tag's up-arrow mark means: your choice for the tag, or its list, moves the result up. In the tag's tooltip and read by screen readers.

tagMarkLower.description: Like tagMarkRaise, for a tag that moves the result down.

tagMarkPin.description: Like tagMarkRaise, for a tag that pins the result to the top.

tagMarkHide.description: Like tagMarkRaise, for a tag that hides the result.

tagMarkSpoken.description: Read by screen readers after a tag's name when the tag moves or hides the result. $1 is tagMarkPin, tagMarkRaise, tagMarkLower, or tagMarkHide.

tagsShowMore.description: In the toolbar popup and the menu on a result: button under a long list of tags that shows the ones folded away. $1 is how many.

tagsShowFewer.description: In the toolbar popup and the menu on a result: the button that folds the extra tags away again, after tagsShowMore.

tagListsPickerHint.message: Adding one changes only your list.
tagListsPickerHint.description: In the toolbar popup and the menu on a result, under tagListsHeading over the tags from lists: adding one of them to a site is saved in your own list, not the list's.

tagFromSource.description: In the toolbar popup and the menu on a result, after the name of a tag a list gave the site, which you can't take off: $1 is the lists, joined.

popupTagFrom.description: $1 is the lists that tag this site.

popupTagSite.description: $1 is a site, $2 a tag's name.

popupTagInvalid.message: Enter a tag name with at least one letter or number.
popupTagInvalid.description: Shown under the new-tag field when its name cannot be used.

popupTagAlreadySet.message: That tag is already on this site.
popupTagAlreadySet.description: Shown when someone tries to add a tag that is already on the current site.

tagSiteReason.message: Why this site fits the “$1” tag (optional)
tagSiteReason.description: Label for an optional explanation when someone adds a site to a tag in Settings.

popupThisPage.description: In the toolbar popup. Heading over what Anubis did on this page, when the engine isn’t known.

popupThisPageOn.description: $1 is a search engine, e.g. Google.

popupNotSearch.message: Search on a supported engine to see what Anubis changes.
popupNotSearch.description: In the toolbar popup. On a page that isn’t a search page.

showHidden.description: Button in the summary above the results and in the toolbar popup: brings back the results Anubis hid on this page.

hideAgain.description: Hides the results Show hidden brought back.

loadMore.description: Button in the summary above the results and in the toolbar popup: adds the next page of results to this one.

loadMoreTitle.message: Add the next page and rank everything together

loading.description: loadMore while the next page loads.

loadMoreEmpty.message: $1 sent no results for page $2, maybe because of a robot check.
loadMoreEmpty.description: In the summary above the results, when Load more results got a page without results. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreRepeat.message: $1 sent page $2 again, so there are no more.
loadMoreRepeat.description: In the summary above the results. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreBusy.message: $1 asked Anubis to slow down before page $2. Try again in a minute.
loadMoreBusy.description: In the summary above the results, when the engine answered “too many requests”. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreRobot.message: $1 wants a robot check before page $2.
loadMoreRobot.description: In the summary above the results, when the engine answered with a robot check (status 403). $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number. loadMoreOpen follows it.

loadMoreRefused.description: In the summary above the results. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreSlow.message: $1 took too long to send page $2.
loadMoreSlow.description: In the summary above the results. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreFailed.description: In the summary above the results, when the request failed. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreOpen.description: Link after loadMoreEmpty and the like: opens the page Anubis tried to load in a new tab. $1 is the page number.

loadMoreOpenTitle.message: Open it in a new tab to see what $1 sent
loadMoreOpenTitle.description: Tooltip of loadMoreOpen. $1 is the search engine.

chipFromPage.description: Under a result's title when Load more results brought it in. $1 is the page number.

barHidden_one.description: In the line standing for hidden results, after the site: “fandom.com hidden”, or “fandom.com and 2 more hidden” for a run of them. $1 is how many results the line stands for.

barHiddenByYou_one.description: Like barHidden, for results hidden by your list. $1 is how many results the line stands for.

barHiddenByTag_one.description: Like barHidden, for results hidden by a tag. $1 is how many results the line stands for; $2 is the tag’s name.

barHiddenByLens_one.description: Like barHidden, for results a list leaves out because it only includes sites it names; $2 is that list. $1 is how many results the line stands for.

barHiddenByList_one.description: Like barHidden, for results a list hides. $1 is how many results the line stands for; $2 is the list’s name.

menuNewTagPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the field in the menu on a result where you name a new tag.

menuNewTagLabel.description: Screen reader label of menuNewTagPlaceholder's field.

menuAddTagButton.description: Button after the new tag field in the menu on a result.

menuTagsMore.description: Button after a site's tags in the menu on a result: shows every tag to choose from, and the field for a new one.

menuTagsDone.description: menuTagsMore while every tag shows: goes back to the site's own tags.

menuCloseLabel.description: Label and tooltip of the × that closes the menu on a result.

anubisSettings.description: Label of the cog button that opens settings, in the toolbar popup, the summary above the results, and the menu on each result.

help.description: In the toolbar popup. Link at the foot to the wiki.

reportProblem.description: Link in the toolbar popup and the settings sidebar that opens a bug report on GitHub.

reportProblemTitle.message: Open a bug report on GitHub, with your version and browser filled in

summaryShowAll.description: In the summary above the results, while only results with one tag are shown.

summaryFilterLabel.description: Screen reader label of the row of tags in the summary above the results.

summaryFilterOn.description: Tooltip of a tag in the summary above the results. $1 is the tag's name.

summaryFilterOff.description: Tooltip of the tag whose results are the only ones shown.

summaryPinned.description: One part of summaryActed: $1 results were pinned. The parts are joined into a list (“pinned 1, raised 2, and hid 2”).

summaryRaised.description: Like summaryPinned, for results that were raised.

summaryLowered.description: Like summaryPinned, for results that were lowered.

summaryHid.description: Like summaryPinned, for results that were hidden.

summaryActed.description: The summary above the results. $1 is the list of summaryPinned, summaryRaised… parts, $2 is summaryResults or summaryResultsPages, e.g. “Anubis raised 1 and hid 2 of 7 results.”

summaryResults_one.description: How many results the page has, for summaryActed.

summaryResultsPages_one.description: Like summaryResults, after Load more results brought in more pages. $2 is the number of pages, always 2 or more.

summaryAlsoRemoved.description: Second sentence of the summary, after summaryActed, when clean-up removed blocks from the page. $1 is the list of summaryRemoved… parts, e.g. “an AI answer and 2 video panels”.

summaryRemovedOnly.description: The summary when clean-up removed blocks but no result was ranked. $1 is as in summaryAlsoRemoved.

summaryShortActed.description: The summary on phones, where the full sentence (summaryActed) takes several lines; Details shows it. $1 is how many results were pinned, raised, lowered, or hidden, $2 is summaryResults or summaryResultsPages, e.g. “Anubis changed 4 of 9 results.”

summaryShortActedRemoved.message: Anubis changed $1 of $2 and cleaned up the page.
summaryShortActedRemoved.description: Like summaryShortActed, when clean-up also removed blocks from the page.

summaryShortRemoved.description: The summary on phones when clean-up removed blocks but no result was ranked; Details shows summaryRemovedOnly.

summaryDetails.description: Button in the summary on phones: shows the full summary, the page's tags, Load more results, and settings.

summaryFewerDetails.description: Button in the summary on phones: folds away what summaryDetails showed.

summaryUnchanged_one.message: Anubis left this result as it was.
summaryUnchanged_one.description: The summary when Anubis changed nothing on a page with one result.

summaryUnchanged_other.message: Anubis left all $1 results as they were.
summaryUnchanged_other.description: The summary when Anubis changed nothing. $1 is the number of results.

summaryUnchangedPages.message: Anubis left all $1 results from $2 pages as they were.
summaryUnchangedPages.description: Like summaryUnchanged, after Load more results brought in more pages. $2 is the number of pages.

summaryFiltered_one.description: The summary while only results with one tag are shown. $1 is the number of results on the page, $2 the tag's name, $3 how many results have it.

summaryRemovedAi_one.description: A part of summaryAlsoRemoved: blocks clean-up removed. $1 is how many.

summaryRemovedDiscussions_one.description: Like summaryRemovedAi, for panels of forum threads.

summaryRemovedNews_one.description: Like summaryRemovedAi, for news panels (“Top stories”).

summaryRemovedImages_one.description: Like summaryRemovedAi, for rows of images.

summaryRemovedRelated_one.description: Like summaryRemovedAi, for lists of related searches.

summaryRemovedMore.description: Last item of the list of removed blocks in the summary when there are too many to name, e.g. “an AI answer, a video panel, a discussions panel, and 2 more”. $1 is how many kinds are left out (at least 2).

summaryRemovedElsewhere_one.message: a row of other search engines
summaryRemovedElsewhere_one.description: Like summaryRemovedAi, for rows of buttons that repeat the search on other engines.

summaryRemovedAdRequests_one.description: Like summaryRemovedAi, for banners asking you to allow ads or turn off an ad blocker.

summaryRemovedAds_one.description: Like summaryRemovedAi, for a block of paid results and product carousels.

withShortcut.description: A button's description followed by its keyboard shortcut, e.g. Show hidden (Alt+Shift+H).

toolbarOff.description: Tooltip of the toolbar button while Anubis is turned off.

weighLabel.description: Tooltip and screen reader label of the balance button on each result, and the name of the menu it opens. $1 is the result's site, e.g. fandom.com.

weighLabelRanked.description: The same label for a site that isn't ranked Normal, whose button shows its ranking. Keep it starting with weighLabel's words. $1 is the site; $2 is chipHidden, chipLowered, chipRaised, or chipPinned in lower case, e.g. “Hide, rank, or tag fandom.com (lowered)”.

hiddenShow.description: Button on the line standing for a hidden result: shows that result.

hiddenShowSite.description: Screen reader label of hiddenShow, naming the site. Keep it starting with hiddenShow's word. $1 is the site, e.g. fandom.com.

hiddenMore_one.description: After a site's name on the one line standing for several hidden results in a row, e.g. “fandom.com and 1 more hidden by your list”.

summaryChangedHide.description: In the summary above the results, after you rank a site from the menu on a result, followed by an Undo button. $1 is the site, e.g. fandom.com.

summaryChangedAllow.description: Like summaryChangedHide, for Normal when a subscribed list ranks the site: it's then ranked Normal whatever the lists say. Normal is the ranking's name, as on the menu's button.

summaryChangedNormal.description: Like summaryChangedHide, after you press the ranking a site already had, so your list no longer ranks it and the subscribed lists decide.

summaryChangedTagOn.description: Like summaryChangedHide, after you tag a site. $1 is the site, $2 the tag's name.

summaryChangedTagOff.description: Like summaryChangedHide, after you untag a site. $1 is the site, $2 the tag's name.

summaryChangedSite.description: Like summaryChangedHide, after several changes to one site's ranking and tags.

summaryUndo.description: Button after summaryChangedHide and the like: puts the site back as it was before. Also after deleting something in Settings: brings it back.

offerTitle.description: Settings → Lists, after a subscribe link opened it. $1 is the list's name.

offerTrust.message: A list can hide, rank, and tag sites. Only subscribe to lists you trust.
offerTrust.description: Settings → Lists, under offerTitle, for a list that isn’t in Anubis’s directory.

offerPermission.message: Your browser will ask to let Anubis read from $1.

offerSubscribe.description: Settings → Lists: the button that subscribes to a list.

offerCancel.description: A button that closes a form without saving, in Settings.

welcomeTitle.description: Tab title of the page that opens when Anubis is installed.

welcomeHeading.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. A small line at the top, beside the logo, before the headline.

welcomeDemoHeading.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Accessible name of the part with the example search page, where you try ranking sites.

welcomeDemoLabel.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Accessible name of the example search results. $1 is welcomeQuery.

welcomeHeadline.message: Choose which sites come first, and which you never see again.
welcomeHeadline.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Its headline: what Anubis is for, in two short sentences.

welcomeLead.message: Anubis puts a small button next to every search result on Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, and others. Have a go on this practice search first. Nothing you do on it is saved.
welcomeLead.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Under welcomeHeadline, beside the practice search on a wide window and above it on a narrow one.

welcomeStepsLabel.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Over the checklist beside the practice search.

welcomeStepOpen.message: Press the button next to a result
welcomeStepOpen.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. A step in the checklist beside the practice search, ticked off once done.

welcomeStepRank.message: Put that site where you want it
welcomeStepRank.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. A step in the checklist beside the practice search, ticked off once done. Choosing Pin, Raise, Lower, or Hide in the menu the button opened.

welcomeStepHide.message: Hide a site you don't want
welcomeStepHide.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. A step in the checklist beside the practice search, ticked off once done.

welcomeStepDone.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Read by screen readers after a step of the checklist that is done.

welcomeStepsAllDone.message: You've done all three. Your real searches work the same way.
welcomeStepsAllDone.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Under the checklist once all three steps are done.

welcomeTourPinned.message: $1 will come first whenever it shows up.
welcomeTourPinned.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. In the tour's third tip, after you pinned a site. $1 is the site.

welcomeTourRaised.message: Anubis will raise $1 whenever it shows up.
welcomeTourRaised.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. In the tour's third tip, after you raised a site rather than pinning it. $1 is the site.

welcomeTourLowered.message: Anubis will lower $1 whenever it shows up.
welcomeTourLowered.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. In the tour's third tip, after you lowered a site rather than pinning it. $1 is the site.

welcomeTourStep.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Before each step of the short tour of the example search page. $1 is the step, $2 how many there are.

welcomeTourOpen.message: Anubis puts this $1 button next to every result. You'd probably trust $2 more than someone's lecture notes, but it's stuck in third. Press the button next to it.
welcomeTourOpen.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. The tour's first tip, under the button beside the third example result. The first result is a student's lecture notes. $1 is the button's small balance icon, and $2 the site, plato.stanford.edu. Written for someone who has never seen Anubis.

welcomeTourRank.message: From here you can move $1 up, down, or off the page. Pin it to keep it at the top.
welcomeTourRank.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. The tour's second tip, under the menu that the button opened, where only Pin can be pressed. Pin is the ranking's name, as on its button (levelPin). $1 is the site, e.g. plato.stanford.edu.

welcomeTourFind.message: Next, find a site you don't want to see and press its $1.
welcomeTourFind.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. The tour's third tip, after you ranked a site, sometimes after welcomeTourPinned, welcomeTourRaised, or welcomeTourLowered. $1 is the button's small balance icon.

welcomeTourHide.message: Press Hide and you won't see $1 again.
welcomeTourHide.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. The tour's third tip, once the menu is open on another site. Hide is the ranking's name, as on its button (levelHide). $1 is the site.

welcomeTourDone.message: It's gone. Anubis always says what it hid above the results, and Undo brings it back. Look for the $1 on your next search.
welcomeTourDone.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. The tour's last tip, under the summary of the example search page, after you hid a site. Undo is the summary's button (summaryUndo). $1 is the button's small balance icon.

welcomeTourGotIt.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. A button on the tour's last tip that closes it.

welcomeTourSkip.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. A button that ends the short tour of the example search page.

welcomeDemoReset.description: A button under the example search results that puts them back in their first order.

welcomeQuery.description: The search shown on the example search page of the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Keep it in English: its example results are English pages, some of which the starter lists tag.

welcomeChoicesHeading.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed: heading over a few switches people often turn on first. Unlike the examples on the page, they change the settings.

welcomeChoicesHow.message: These change your settings straight away. Change them again in Settings whenever you like.
welcomeChoicesHow.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Under welcomeChoicesHeading.

welcomeChoiceAi.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed: a switch, the same as Settings → Remove panels → AI answers.

welcomeChoiceAiHint.message: Google’s AI Overview, Duck.ai, and the AI answers on Bing and Brave.
welcomeChoiceAiHint.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed: under welcomeChoiceAi.

welcomeChoiceAiSites.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed: a switch that sets the tag “AI-generated” to Hide in Settings → Tags.

welcomeChoiceAiSitesHint.message: Sites the AI content list tags as AI-generated.
welcomeChoiceAiSitesHint.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed: under welcomeChoiceAiSites. “AI content” is the name of a list.

welcomeChoicePaywalls.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed: a switch that sets the tag “Paywalled” to Lower in Settings → Tags.

welcomeChoicePaywallsHint.message: News and magazine sites with a paywall move five places down.
welcomeChoicePaywallsHint.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed: under welcomeChoicePaywalls.

welcomeMoreHeading.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Heading over short examples of tags, lists, and removing panels, each opened on its own.

welcomeMoreHow.message: You don't need any of these, but each one is worth a look.
welcomeMoreHow.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Under welcomeMoreHeading.

welcomeTagsHeading.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Opens the example of tags.

welcomeTagsWhat.message: Put your own labels on sites.
welcomeTagsWhat.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Beside welcomeTagsHeading.

welcomeTagsHow.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Over a few example tags to put on an example search result.

welcomeTagNotes.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. An example tag to put on a search result, a site of students' notes.

welcomeTagSignUp.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. An example tag to put on a search result, for sites that make you sign up to read them. Like the others, a tag you could make yourself; this one lowers the sites that have it.

welcomeTagTrusted.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. An example tag to put on a search result. This one raises the sites that have it.

welcomeTagsMore.message: A tag can move every site that has it. Trusted raises them and Sign-up wall lowers them.
welcomeTagsMore.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. After the example of tags. Trusted and Sign-up wall are welcomeTagTrusted and welcomeTagSignUp.

welcomeTagsOpen.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. A button that opens Settings → Tags.

welcomeListsTitle.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Opens the example of lists.

welcomeListsWhat.message: Use lists that other people keep up to date.
welcomeListsWhat.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Beside welcomeListsTitle.

welcomeListsHow.message: Switch these off and on to see the tags change.
welcomeListsHow.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Over a few example lists, each with a switch, beside example search results.

welcomeListsCount_one.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. After the example of lists. $1 is how many lists you subscribe to.

welcomeListsHeading.description: Heading over the lists you subscribe to, on the welcome page and in Settings → Lists.

welcomeListsMore.message: You can turn them off or add more in the settings.
welcomeListsMore.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. After the lists you start with.

welcomeListsOpen.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. A button that opens Settings → Lists.

welcomePanelsHeading.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Opens the example of removing panels, such as AI answers, from search pages.

welcomePanelsWhat.message: Get rid of AI answers and other clutter.
welcomePanelsWhat.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Beside welcomePanelsHeading.

welcomePanelsExample.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Heading of an example AI answer on the example search page.

welcomePanelsMore.message: Anubis leaves these alone until you say otherwise. Pick what to remove in the settings.
welcomePanelsMore.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. After the example of removing panels.

welcomePanelsOpen.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. A button that opens Settings → Remove panels.

welcomePinHeading.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Heading of the part about Anubis's button in the browser's toolbar, which is optional.

welcomePinWhy.message: You don't need it, but it's handy. It lets you rank the site you're on and see what Anubis did to a search.
welcomePinWhy.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. Under welcomePinHeading, before the steps to put the button on the toolbar.

welcomePinChrome.message: Press the puzzle piece next to the address bar, then the pin beside Anubis.
welcomePinChrome.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. How to keep Anubis’s button on the toolbar in this browser. Use the names the browser shows in your language. For Chrome.

welcomePinEdge.message: Press the puzzle piece next to the address bar, then the eye beside Anubis.
welcomePinEdge.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. How to keep Anubis’s button on the toolbar in this browser. Use the names the browser shows in your language. For Edge.

welcomePinOpera.message: Press the cube next to the address bar, then the pin beside Anubis.
welcomePinOpera.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. How to keep Anubis’s button on the toolbar in this browser. Use the names the browser shows in your language. For Opera.

welcomePinFirefox.message: Press the puzzle piece, then the gear beside Anubis, and choose Pin to Toolbar.
welcomePinFirefox.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. How to keep Anubis’s button on the toolbar in this browser. Use the names the browser shows in your language. For Firefox on a computer.

welcomePinAndroid.message: Anubis is in the browser's menu, under Extensions.
welcomePinAndroid.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. For Firefox for Android, which has no toolbar for extensions. Use the names Firefox shows in your language.

welcomePinned.description: Shown instead of the steps once the browser says the button is pinned.

welcomeGuide.description: A link to the wiki, on the welcome page and in the settings sidebar.

welcomePrivacy.description: On the page that opens when Anubis is installed. A link to the privacy policy.

syncHeading.description: Settings → Sync: the section’s heading, also in the sidebar.

syncIntro.message: Your sites and settings on your other computers and browsers.

syncBrowserHeading.description: Settings → Sync: heading over the browser’s own sync.

syncFirefox.message: Firefox syncs your sites and settings when you're signed in with Add-ons ticked in its sync settings.
